notes: Push-up variants now use PUBLISHED force-plate measurements instead of one flat number. Percentage of bodyweight carried by the hands: flat 64-66 percent with two independent studies agreeing, knee push-up 49-52.5 percent, and across hand and foot elevation the measured range is about 41 to 74 percent. Flat stays 0.64, knee 0.51, hands-elevated 0.55, feet-elevated 0.74

Watch the naming trap: for push-ups incline means HANDS elevated and is EASIER, decline means FEET elevated and is HARDER - the opposite of your bench crunch. The rules match on the direction word, never a shared incline pattern, so your incline crunch stays the hard 0.85 case and an incline bench press is still not bodyweight at all
